We correctly detected a strong, replicated, dose-dependent cytoskeletal phenotype: act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 at 10 uM (e2) and +19.4 at 3 uM (e4) with Spearman rho=+1.00 (e8), replicated in rep2 (e11, e12), plus low solidity/stellate morphology confirmed visually (e6) and no mitotic arrest (e10). We misattributed this actin remodeling to direct Actin disruptors because the reference atlas plurality was Actin disruptors 3/10 (e7) and we over-weighted actin texture channels. In hindsight bryostatin is a PKC-pathway modulator (PMID 22539107, PMID 2697470), and kinase signaling through PKC/PKD (PMID 7785505, PMID 18765827) can remodel the cytoskeleton downstream and thus phenocopy direct actin poisons at the level of texture and solidity. Our targeted literature search for bryostatin-actin morphology returned 0 hits (e17), so we lacked that link in-run and kept Kinase inhibitors at 0.0025.

The acquisition choices reinforced the error: we repeatedly acquired high-dose wells (10 uM, 3 uM, 1 uM with replicates) measuring the same act_std/act_glcm_contrast and solidity features rather than an orthogonal readout. We discounted the large tubulin co-signal (tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6 in e2, tub_std z=+19.3 in e11) as secondary shape change and never tested reversibility, PKC translocation/phosphorylation, or cell-free actin polymerization that would separate upstream kinase modulation from direct filament disruption.

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

We correctly detected a strong, replicated, dose-dependent cytoskeletal phenotype: act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 at 10 uM (e2) and +19.4 at 3 uM (e4) with Spearman rho=+1.00 (e8), replicated in rep2 (e11, e12), plus low solidity/stellate morphology confirmed visually (e6) and no mitotic arrest (e10). That correctly ruled out microtubule/Aurora/Eg5 arrest phenotypes.

We misattributed this actin remodeling to direct Actin disruptors because the reference atlas plurality was Actin disruptors 3/10 (e7) and we over-weighted actin texture channels. In hindsight bryostatin is a PKC-pathway modulator (PMID 22539107, PMID 2697470), and kinase signaling through PKC/PKD (PMID 7785505, PMID 18765827) can remodel the cytoskeleton downstream and thus phenocopy direct actin poisons at the level of texture and solidity. Our targeted literature search for bryostatin-actin morphology returned 0 hits (e17), so we lacked that link in-run and kept Kinase inhibitors at 0.0025.

The acquisition choices reinforced the error: we repeatedly acquired high-dose wells (10 uM, 3 uM, 1 uM with replicates) measuring the same act_std/act_glcm_contrast and solidity features rather than an orthogonal readout. We discounted the large tubulin co-signal (tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6 in e2, tub_std z=+19.3 in e11) as secondary shape change and never tested reversibility, PKC translocation/phosphorylation, or cell-free actin polymerization that would separate upstream kinase modulation from direct filament disruption.

What was right:
- Identified a real dose-dependent cytoskeletal effect: extreme act_glcm_contrast and act_std at 10 uM and 3 uM with monotonic dose response (e2, e4, e8) and replication across reps (e11, e12).
- Detected stellate/low-solidity morphology with lower density visually (e6) and quantitatively (cell_solidity z=-15.9 in e4, negative trend e9).
- Correctly rejected mitotic-arrest MoAs by showing no increase in frac_mitotic_like across doses (e10, rho=-0.95).

What was wrong or missed:
- Assigned direct Actin disruptors (p=0.72) instead of Kinase inhibitors; bryostatin-driven PKC signaling phenocopied actin disruption in texture/solidity features.
- Over-relied on atlas plurality Actin disruptors 3/10 (e7) and microscopist candidate Actin disruptors (e6) while leaving Kinase inhibitors at 0.0025 without a kinase-specific test.
- Dismissed tubulin co-elevation (e2, e11-e12) and reduced nuc_dna_mean/eccentricity at 0.3-1 uM (e3, e5) as secondary, missing a broader signaling effect rather than pure actin poisoning.

Proposed next experiment: Test PKC-dependence of the stellate actin phenotype in cells with phalloidin imaging plus a PKC translocation/phospho-substrate readout with bryostatin +/- a PKC inhibitor, run in parallel with a cell-free actin polymerization assay to rule out direct actin binding as in cytochalasins.
